description:
FOUND s470bw (2026-09-06), probing #1261's reproducer against perl 5.40.3.

REPRO (B2.pm and A2.pm in one directory, PERL5LIB pointing at it):

  package B2;
  use Exporter 'import';
  our @EXPORT = qw(blk);
  sub blk { return ref($_[0]) . ":" . scalar(@_) }   # NO prototype
  1;

  package A2;
  use B2;
  sub go { return blk { 42 } }
  1;

  perl : HASH:1     -- `{ 42 }` is an anonymous hash constructor, so blk gets
                       one argument, a HASH ref
  PCL  : :1         -- ref($_[0]) is "" : the emission is `(A2::pl-blk 42)`,
                       i.e. the BLOCK'S VALUE, and the hash is never built

Same family as #478 (which was about a `(&)`/`(&@)` prototype not crossing a
`use`, so a block-form call got the block's value instead of a code ref).  This
is the OTHER half: with no prototype at all, perl does not make a block-form
call â it parses `{ â¦ }` as a TERM, an anon hash â and PCL still unwraps it.

WITH a `(&@)` prototype PCL is right (`CODE:1`, probed on the same fixture), and
with an EMPTY `()` prototype the term rule is right too (#365/#453, probed:
`zap + 1` is 8 with `sub zap ()` and 107 without, both matching perl).  So the
gap is exactly "declared sub, no prototype, followed by a brace block".

Not fixed in s470bw: it is a PExpr term-grammar question, not a cache one, and
#1261's acceptance rows use the `()`-prototype and export facts instead (both
perl-equal on both sides).  The `(&@)` fixture is preserved in that session's
scratch reproducer (scratch/s470bw/repro) as the demonstration.
subject: A DECLARED sub with NO prototype followed by a block: perl builds an anonymous HASH (`blk { 42 }` == blk({42})), PCL passes the BLOCK'S VALUE (`(pl-blk 42)`) -- silent wrong, the #478 residue with no prototype at all
